finding: Attempting to maintain activity was linked to less impairment; accommodating and behavioural disengagement were linked to more impairment and distress, with causal direction unclear.
At slow speeds CFS patients showed altered hip and knee angles and shorter relative stride length, and ran 30 m more slowly than sedentary controls.
Baseline cortisol was lowest in CFS, intermediate in controls and highest in depression (P=0.01); prolactin response to d-fenfluramine was higher in CFS than controls (P=0.05).
63% had improved, 6% were symptom-free, 30% could not work; cell-mediated immune function at entry or follow-up did not predict outcome.
South African expert-consensus guideline on CFS diagnosis and management, with disputes over whether CFS is a distinct illness.
Telephone interview of a community sample found CFS prevalence 0.2% with a more rigorous method.
Illness behaviour questionnaire profiles were identical in CFS and multiple sclerosis, so they are not evidence of abnormal illness behaviour.
CFS patients in the area hit hardest by Hurricane Andrew had more physician-rated relapses and symptom increases than those in less-affected areas; distress response was the strongest predictor.
Enteroviral 5'NTR sequences from CFS patients clustered separately, and 19 of 20 were distinct from known enteroviruses, interpreted as persistent infection.
note: No controls; later PCR studies were negative

finding: Chronic fatigue was reported by 19% of an HMO sample but only 3 of 74 enrolled persons met CDC CFS criteria.

n: 35 vs 30 pain vs 34 organic vs 34 neurotic
finding: CFS patients described themselves as more action-prone before illness than organic and neurotic groups, similar to chronic pain.
Sequencing indicated a cytopathic 'stealth virus' cultured from a CFS patient was closest to simian cytomegalovirus, implicating an African green monkey origin.
note: Single isolate; stealth virus claims not confirmed

finding: Patients without psychiatric disorder had milder illness; there were no viral or immunological differences between psychiatric subgroups.
Community postal survey found 4 CFS cases (0.56%, 95% CI 0.16-1.47%) and strong association of fatigue with psychological morbidity.
70% of GPs were reluctant to give a CFS diagnosis whereas patients valued a coherent diagnosis.
HHV-7 DNA was present in over 80% of CFS and controls, while HHV-6 variant A was more common in CFS (22% vs 4%, P=0.05).
Hypothesis that chronic intestinal candidiasis depresses T and NK cell function and may cause CFS.
Vagal power during paced breathing was lower in CFS overall (p<0.034) and at most breathing rates and postures.
Bone marrow morphology, PCR and serology showed no clinically important parvovirus B19 infection in 7 selected CFS patients.
note: No controls; selected for most likely infection

finding: EBV load (spontaneous transformation) and immunologic regression assay did not differ from healthy controls, even in patients with high VCA and EA titres.
Patent for measuring body phosphate stores (AMP, ADP, ATP) in urine or plasma to diagnose ME/PVFS and treating with phosphate.
P300 amplitude and latency (and N1, P2, N2) did not differ from matched controls across target probabilities.
Of 11 immunological tests, protein A binding, Raji cell and C3/C4 deviations discriminated best; IgG subclasses, CH50, IL-2 and anticardiolipin did not.
Fatigue and sleepiness were moderately correlated (r=0.63) and both groups reported sleep problems, mainly quality not amount.
Prolactin and cortisol responses to dl-fenfluramine did not differ from controls, giving no support for altered 5-HT function.
Prolactin response to hypoglycaemia was attenuated, ACTH response greater (36.4 vs 25.6 pg/ml) with unchanged cortisol, suggesting pituitary and adrenal cortical impairment.
Overall neuropsychological performance in CFS matched depressed patients and was below MS and controls, with information processing speed most impaired.
Patients giving catastrophic answers about pushing beyond limits had higher fatigue and greater disability.
Blinded quantified electron microscopy of muscle biopsies found no difference in mitochondrial aggregates, size, pleomorphism or compartmentalisation.
note: Blinded; contradicts the Italian biopsy report

finding: Vestibular testing showed no single pattern but poor dynamic posturography and lower earth-vertical rotation gain, suggesting central rather than peripheral deficits.
Serum total carnitine, free carnitine and acylcarnitine were significantly lower in CFS and correlated with functional capacity.
A simian CMV-related stealth virus from a CFS patient caused acute encephalopathy in inoculated cats.
note: Animal; stealth virus not independently confirmed

finding: Antibodies to EBV (including ZEBRA), HHV-6 and HHV-7 were higher in CFS patients than controls.
note: Small; atlas finds standard serology does not separate large cohorts

finding: Review of CFS research on immune, hypothalamic-pituitary, neurotransmitter and cerebral perfusion abnormalities.
International study group's 1994 revised case definition and evaluation guidelines for chronic fatigue syndrome (Fukuda criteria).
note: Defines the Fukuda criteria used in later studies

finding: Total T, CD4 and CD8 counts did not differ, but CD3-CD16+ and CD57+CD56+ NK cells were reduced, other NK subsets expanded, with higher adhesion and activation markers on NK cells.
No difference in enterovirus serology or VP1 antigen, and no enterovirus isolated from stool cultures; one patient had a PCR-positive stool not reproduced 3 months later.
NK cell activity and CD16+/CD56+ counts were significantly lower in CFS (p<0.01) and in non-CFS chronic fatigue, with more life stress and sleep disturbance.
Title only: corticospinal excitability study in CFS; no abstract.
Of 63 Italian patients with persistent fatigue, alternative diagnoses were made in 59% and only 6 met CDC CFS criteria.
Patients in all three diagnostic groups reported more fatigue and lower perceived health than controls; CFS and MS also had lower activity.
Overall neuropsychological performance in CFS matched depressed patients and both were within normal limits on most measures.
CFS, FM and MCS groups were similar in demographics and symptoms; 70% of FM and 30% of MCS met CFS criteria.
Red cell magnesium did not differ from matched normals and magnesium loading tests showed no deficiency.

EBV VCA IgG at 1:320 or higher in 55% vs 15%; EA, HHV-6 and HSV titres did not differ; coxsackie B1 and B4 antibodies were higher; elevations were largely not coincident, arguing for nonspecific immune activation.
In 87 patients with prolonged low-grade fever, 45 were asymptomatic by 3 years; the syndrome was proposed as a CFS variant.
In vitro IL-2 and interferon-gamma production were higher in CFS; all other immune measures similar, and no causal link to abnormal immunity was found.
MUGA scans in 11 CFS patients showed abnormal wall motion at rest and stress, left ventricular dilatation and segmental abnormalities.
note: No controls; contrasts with later smaller LV findings

finding: Debate on the CDC case definition, infection and allergy roles, psychiatric confounding and diagnostic tests.
Postal questionnaires yielded nine dimensions of CFS including functional impairment, sleep disturbance, avoidance, neuropsychological impairment and self-efficacy.
Men and women with CFS differed little clinically or psychosocially; women more often had tender or enlarged lymph nodes (60% vs 33%).
CFS had more depressive symptoms but less cognitive impairment than MS; a subset did poorly on visuomotor search and logical memory.
Baseline bioactive 2-5A (p<0.0001) and RNase L activity (p=0.001) were elevated; poly(I)-poly(C12U) lowered both in those with high baseline, correlating with cognitive improvement.
note: Sponsor-linked RNase L biomarker study; n not given

finding: Patent for a vitamin and mineral composition (methionine, magnesium, folate, B6, B12) for CFS.

Long-term prognosis was good for those who responded to treatment, spontaneous recovery was unlikely in non-responders, and persistent CFS linked to more somatic disorder and prior psychiatric history.
Case report of a 13-year-old with bipolar disorder initially assumed to have post-viral fatigue syndrome.
MRI showed more T2-bright white matter foci in CFS (2.06 vs 0.80 per subject), with SPECT abnormalities, in the same patients.
note: Atlas finds conventional MRI does not separate groups; small

n: 45 CFS vs 27 AIDS dementia vs 14 depression vs 38 healthy
finding: HMPAO SPECT defects per patient were 6.53 in CFS vs 1.66 in controls (similar to depression 6.43), and midcerebral uptake index was lower in CFS.
note: Authors favoured chronic viral encephalitis; not specific to CFS

finding: At 3.2 years 65 had improved but only 6 had no symptoms; physical-cause beliefs and primary psychiatric diagnosis predicted poor outcome, immune function did not.
All 25 CFS patients had ocular symptoms; tear film and surface abnormalities in 19 and reduced accommodation in 18.

After 30 min slow walking, IL-1 beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were undetectable; resting serum TGF-beta was higher in CFS (287 vs 115 pg/ml), and post-exercise TGF-beta and SPECT blood flow changes were larger but not significant versus controls.
Review proposing mild adrenocortical deficiency in chronic allergies, autoimmunity and unexplained chronic fatigue, based on old reports of benefit from physiological cortisol doses.
Argues from limited epidemiology that the 'yuppie flu' stereotype of CFS derives from treatment-based studies.
Review of epidemic neuromyasthenia outbreaks showing inconsistent case definitions and variable, infrequent cases meeting CFS criteria.
Serum acylcarnitine was low in Japanese CFS patients and tended to normalise with recovery from fatigue.
CFS patients were worse than controls on many cognitive tests, most markedly psychomotor tests; some measures improved over time; memory differences resembled Crohn's controls.
CFS CD8+ T cells had reduced CD11b and raised CD38 and HLA-DR, and NK activity was markedly decreased in almost all patients; T, B and NK numbers were normal.
Enterovirus RNA by PCR in muscle was found in 26.4% of CFS and 19.8% of other neuromuscular disease, not significant, unlike the earlier smaller study (53% vs 15%).
Review concluding that impaired information processing rather than primary memory dysfunction underlies CFS cognitive problems.
CFS patients scored higher on hypochondriasis and disease conviction than general practice patients, and 66.7% scored above the GHQ-28 cut-off.
61% met CDC, 55% British and 56% Australian criteria, and laboratory abnormalities were similar across groups including those meeting none.
Negative automatic thoughts and disengagement coping correlated with illness burden in CFS regardless of depression diagnosis.
Review of skin manifestations in CFS (aphthous stomatitis, EBV-related erythema multiforme) and CDC criteria.

27 women from a CFS clinic had a Sjogren-like illness: abnormal Schirmer test in 16/27, abnormal minor salivary gland biopsy in 20/25, ANA in 16/27 but anti-Ro in 1/21; 18/27 met 6+ CDC minor criteria.
note: Clinic selection; no controls; abstract truncated

finding: 8 of 27 children with CFS (29.6%) also met fibromyalgia criteria and had more muscle pain, sleep disturbance and neurological symptoms.
HHV-6 DNA was found in PBMC of 7 of 13 CFS patients (4 variant A, 3 variant B) and no controls, with higher HHV-6 antibody titres.
note: Small; conflicts with other cohorts that found no difference

finding: Severe fatigue with neurological complaints was seen in 90%, 23% and 10% of respondents in three sick-building outbreaks.

Immune tests showed abnormal lymphocyte stimulation in 50%, low IgG3 in 59% and IgG1 in 11%, circulating immune complexes in 42%, raised TNF-alpha in 47%, autoantibodies, and EBV-EA positive/low EBNA pattern in 78%.
note: German; no control group in abstract

finding: PCR and Southern blot for HTLV-I/II, spuma, simian, bovine, feline and gibbon retroviruses were negative in all patients and controls.
No change in plasma interferon-gamma, interferon-alpha, IL-1 beta or TNF-alpha before, during or 24 h after 30 min of grip exercise; fatigue and mood scores improved.
Nevada cancer registry review found no consistent non-Hodgkin lymphoma trend after a CFS-like outbreak and a brain/CNS tumour rise in line with national trend.

12-28% had TNF-alpha, TNF-beta, IL-1 alpha, IL-2, sIL-2R or neopterin above control 95th percentile and only TNF-alpha and TNF-beta distributions differed overall; mediators correlated with each other in patients only.
Point prevalence of CFS was 0.3% (CDC), 0.4% (British) and 1.0% (Australian) in an urban primary care practice.
Higher rates of CFS-related symptoms among nurses than previous epidemiological studies.
Brain MRI was abnormal in 27% of CFS vs 2% of controls (T2 white matter foci in 9 vs 1, ventricular or sulcal enlargement in 5).
note: Controls had headache or head trauma; other cohorts found no difference

finding: Review stating CFS is rare as CDC-defined, frequently preceded by depression or anxiety, and overlaps with neurasthenia.
All 24 CFS patients had abnormal T wave patterns on Holter vs 22.4% of others (p<0.01); stress MUGA showed left ventricular dysfunction in 8 of 60 CFS patients.
Patent proposing arsenic trioxide as a treatment for CFS.
note: Patent; no data and unsafe claim

finding: Patients reported more attention difficulty and cognitive symptoms but objective focused attention tests were not clearly impaired, with psychomotor slowing on Stroop reading and naming.
Quadriceps force, relaxation rate and recovery to 48 h were normal after incremental cycling, while perceived exertion for a given heart rate was higher, suggesting central limits.
Essay using one patient's recovery story to argue for psychoneuroimmunology and community psychology approaches.
Patients were slower on psychomotor tasks, had increased visual sensitivity, impaired attention and slower semantic retrieval and reasoning, not explained by psychopathology.
An illness management questionnaire yielded four coping factors that together predicted about a quarter of variance in impairment, anxiety and depression.
HHV-6 antibody titre was higher in CDC-defined CFS than in fatigue not meeting criteria (1:99 vs 1:15, P=0.007), other serology similar.
Mild memory impairment only on tasks needing conceptually driven encoding and retrieval, unrelated to precipitating illness or fatigue.
CFS patients spent more time in bed (544 vs 465 min) and most had sleep disorders on polysomnography.
90% of responding Otago GPs accepted CFS as a valid diagnosis.
Children with CFS had higher fatigue and depressive scores than cystic fibrosis and healthy controls and seriously disrupted schooling.
Cognitive battery comparing CFS, MS and healthy controls for information processing; abstract is cut off before results.
In a blinded controlled CDC study, three commercial retroviral serology/PCR tests did not distinguish CFS patients from healthy controls.
Pilot action research on acceptable service delivery models for CFS in general practice.
HTLV-II gag sequence was not found in any patient or control, and transfusion and sexual-risk exposures did not differ.
HTLV-II gag, simian T-cell leukaemia virus, human spumavirus, bovine leukaemia virus and simian retrovirus were not detected and did not distinguish cases from controls.
CFS had lower CD4 percentage and naive CD4 cells, increased adhesion markers on memory CD4 cells, and reduced mitogen proliferation; similar changes in non-CDC fatigue patients.

Muscle light and electron microscopy showed no consistent relation between symptoms and fibre type, degeneration, glycogen or mitochondria; contractile function was normal at rest and 48 h recovery; perceived exertion was higher.
note: Authors conclude CFS is not a myopathy

finding: Hypothesis paper proposing histamine hypersensitivity, electrolyte and mitochondrial disturbances and T3/insulin dysfunction in CFS.
During intense sustained tibialis contraction voluntary activation was lower in CFS while fatigability, metabolism and M-wave were normal, indicating a central component of muscle fatigue.
26% of referred patients met the CFS case definition; 45% had prior psychiatric history; minimum prevalence 2.0-7.3 per 100,000 across four cities.
All 30 Japanese CFS patients were seronegative for HTLV-II, HTLV-I and HIV, PCR negative for HTLV-II, and no retrovirus grew from PBMC co-culture.
Psychiatric diagnoses explained chronic fatigue in 74% and physical disorders in 7%; 30% met CFS criteria and had more somatization disorder and viral attribution than other chronic fatigue.
Over 4 years few fibromyalgia patients developed a new somatic disease; most reported severe fatigue but only one fifth met CFS criteria.
CFS patients had less depression and fewer personality disorders than major depression, and more current depression than MS after illness onset.
Patent for EEG delta-wave phase reversal as a CFS marker and biofeedback to reduce slow-wave activity.
PCR/Southern blot for HTLV I/II gag, pol, env, tax gave no difference from controls and sera were negative for human foamy virus.
78% of Japanese CFS patients had allergies, mostly cutaneous and drug allergy, and immune tests did not correlate with allergy status.
Plasma MHPG was lower and 5-HIAA higher in CFS, with CSF monoamine metabolites also measured.
Japanese hospital series: some had NK dysfunction, EBV antibody elevation and low arachidonic acid; 98 of 134 returned to work or school on Kampo medicine.
Series of 51 Japanese cases (78% women), 77.5% with flu-like onset, no specific laboratory pattern, ANF positive in 31%, 56.8% improved.
Tender points in all but two patients; EBV VCA IgG higher (p<0.0015), HHV-6 IgG and NK activity not different, NK cell number (CD57) lower (p<0.005).
note: NK activity normal but NK number low

finding: Nevada registry showed no significant non-Hodgkin lymphoma increase attributable to the 1984-86 CFS outbreak.
HMPAO SPECT showed lower cortical/cerebellar ratios across multiple regions (P<0.05), with at least one reduced region in 80% of patients.
Nested PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in blood was sensitive and specific; only incidental mention of ME-like illness.
Herbal and homeopathic preparations produced no significant change in symptoms or lymphocyte markers in 6 outpatients.
Nursing review of the physical versus psychological controversy and care suggestions.
Enterovirus VP1 antigen was positive in 11/34 CFS vs 7/34 depressed (ns); Monospot positive in 4 CFS only; neither test discriminated.
Only 1 of 13,538 Epidemiologic Catchment Area respondents met approximated CDC CFS criteria, though 23% reported persistent fatigue.
Event-related potentials (N1, P2, N2, P300) and short-term memory performance did not differ, though patients had slower and more variable reaction times.
Psychiatric diagnosis, functional disability and symptom amplification rose linearly with the number of lifetime medically unexplained symptoms, questioning the multiple-symptom requirement.
After 3 years almost all cases in four Nevada-California clusters returned to pre-illness activity; no link to EBV, HHV-6 or HTLV; giardiasis preceded one cluster.
NIH workshop recommended relaxing psychiatric exclusions in the CDC case definition, standard laboratory panel, subgrouping, and noted no confirmatory test.
Patent for diagnosing CFS by raised CD8+ cells expressing CD38 or HLA-DR or lower CD11b on CD8+ cells.
In a placebo-controlled trial of high-dose IVIG, only the active group showed correlated improvement in depressive symptoms and cell-mediated immunity markers.
All CFS patients had unrefreshing sleep and a prominent alpha-EEG NREM sleep anomaly (p<=0.001), with no EBV antibody difference, more tender points and depressive symptoms.
Soluble IL-2, soluble CD8 and neopterin were raised in acute mononucleosis but not CFS; IL-1 alpha was higher in both.
Patent for peptide T-like peptides as treatment for CFS.
Overview of ME as a post-viral syndrome with prevalence 1.3 per 1000 and female:male 1.8:1.
Factor analysis gave four symptom components; fatigue, somatic and cognitive components related to illness severity while emotional distress did not.
Two severe childhood CFS cases discussed in psychopathological terms with recovery after treatment.
Combined EA-R and EA-D antibody titres were higher in patients (P<0.001) but not useful individually, and high-titre patients were clinically similar.
Title only: chronic primary magnesium deficiency in CFS; no abstract.
EBV early antigen IgG was higher in definite CFS than probable cases and controls, and an EA-IgG/EBNA ratio correlated with fatigue.
ME patients performed worse on two verbal memory tests and scored lower on extraversion and psychoticism.
Review sorting 32 papers into confirmed (mild humoral immune abnormalities, depression, personality) and contradictory (herpes, enterovirus, cellular immunity, IVIG) findings.
CFS patients had impaired lymphocyte PHA responses and reduced or absent delayed-type hypersensitivity versus both depressed patients and healthy controls (P<0.05).

Evening plasma cortisol (89.0 vs 148.4 nmol/L, P<0.01) and 24-h urinary free cortisol (122.7 vs 203.1 nmol/24 h, P<0.0002) were lower, with elevated basal evening ACTH, indicating impaired HPA activation.
note: Foundational HPA study; abstract truncated before CRH-challenge results

finding: Psychological distress was common on rating scales but specific psychiatric diagnoses were uncommon; no consistently abnormal biochemical or immune indices.
CFS patients had psychiatric disorder rates (78%) similar to fatigued controls but more somatization disorder and physical attribution.
Review of CFS and fibromyalgia criteria, epidemiology and management in adolescents.

n: 147 vs 80 healthy vs 22 contacts vs 43 disease
finding: CFS showed a reduced CD8 suppressor population and raised CD38 and HLA-DR on CD8 cells, absent in healthy, contacts and disease controls, unrelated to viral serology.
Guideline-style paper on antidepressant use for depression in CFS.
GPs estimated CFS prevalence at 1.3 per 1000 patients, female:male 1.8:1, with peak in ages 30-44.
Psychiatric disorder was more common in CFS (41% cases) than muscle disease (12.5%), relative risk 3.3.
Serum bioactive TGF-beta was higher (290 vs 104 pg/mL, P<0.01) and LPS-stimulated PBMC release of IL-1 beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha was higher, while TGF-beta release was lower.
IgM immune complexes, Con A and Coxsackie B proliferation, and Coxsackie B and other viral antibodies did not differ from normal or dystrophy controls.
Clinical review of CFS and depression in adolescents emphasising developmental issues and psychiatric referral.
Anti-hepatitis C antibody was positive in 1 of 36 CFS patients and 0 of 14 controls.
Patent for peptide T-like peptides for CFS.
91% had an acute infection-like onset; at 1 year none had fully recovered but about 40% improved on each symptom.
CFS overlapped with chronic pain on symptoms and MMPI scales and showed raised emotionality, interpreted as predisposing.

In 35 German post-infectious CFS patients followed up to 8 years, HHV-6 activity was seen in 73% and EBV in 34%, immune tests were inconsistent and no treatment gave consistent benefit, IVIG seeming best.
Patent for diagnosing CFS by ambulatory ECG monitoring of non-positive T waves.
Nursing article on recognising ME and advising rest.
Practical review stating psychiatric conditions are often involved, extensive virology and unorthodox treatments lack evidence, and placebo response is strong.
CD16, CD56 and CD57 NK cells were reduced, CD4 ICAM-1+ T cells and monocyte ICAM-1/LFA-1 raised, antigen-specific proliferation and pneumococcal vaccine response reduced; 40% had raised anti-HHV-6.
Spontaneous lymphocyte transformation by EBV occurred in 30% of patients vs 8% of seropositive controls, with antibodies to lytic proteins more frequent in patients.
Open CBT trial with optional antidepressants improved disability, fatigue and symptoms; outcome depended on strength of exclusively physical attribution, not illness length.
Central activation (93.6% vs 90.9%), voluntary and stimulated torque decline and perceived effort during 45 min of submaximal isometric exercise did not differ from controls.
Commentary on EBV nuclear antigen antibody deficiency, stress and postinfectious neurasthenia in CFS pathogenesis.
21 of 33 fibromyalgia patients had significant fatigue but only 7 met CFS criteria; painful glands or fever distinguished CFS.
Summary of Nevada cluster findings: lymphadenopathy, cognitive loss, abnormal brain MRI, low EBNA antibody, high EA-R antibody, raised CD4/CD8 ratio and HHV-6 association.
Commentary calling for exploratory data analysis and data synthesis methods in CFS research.
In a school cluster, relative risks were high for symptoms in family members, raw milk and allergy history.
Proposal for prospective studies of fatigue after known viral infections measuring virus burden, strain and immune recognition.
93 of 100 consecutive patients labelled ME/PVS had time course and respiratory psychophysiology characteristic of chronic habitual hyperventilation.
note: Single clinic; author attributes illness to hyperventilation

finding: Point prevalence in an Australian valley was 37.1 per 100,000, F:M 1.3:1, with 43% unable to attend work or school.
CFS patients had shorter treadmill time, higher submaximal heart rate, higher blood lactate at stage III and higher Borg scores than normal or IBS controls.
Coxsackie B neutralising titres were significant in 50% (103/205) and enteroviral IgM positive in 31% (38/124) of patients referred with ME.
Enteroviral RNA found in CFS muscle biopsies had approximately equal positive and negative strands, unlike lytic infection, suggesting defective control of persistent viral RNA synthesis.
note: Later muscle PCR studies were negative; n not given

finding: Premorbid psychiatric disorder rates in CFS did not exceed community estimates and psychiatric symptoms differed from depression, suggesting disturbance is a consequence.
Brainstem, somatosensory and visual evoked potentials were normal but N2 and P3 latencies and reaction times were prolonged, with abnormal P3 in 36-48% of VP1 positive patients.
Historical comparison of neurasthenia and ME, arguing both need psychosocial and neurobiological explanation.
Patients scored better than age norms on concentration, attention and abstraction tests despite subjective cognitive complaints.
note: Compared with published norms; n not given

finding: Patent for low-dose naltrexone or naloxone to treat chronic herpes infections, CFS, rheumatoid arthritis and MS.
Most CFS patients have a fibromyalgia-like tender point examination, suggesting shared mechanisms including viral immune dysfunction.
Patent for essential fatty acids to treat post-viral fatigue syndrome.
85% of patients had monocyte dysfunction (fewer vimentin-positive cells, low phagocytosis, reduced HLA-DR) that improved after incubation with naloxone; lymphocyte blastogenesis was low.
Compares clinical presentation of ME with and without laboratory evidence of infection and discusses diagnostic criteria.
Magazine article on CFS in elite athletes and overtraining.
Magazine article on the search for the cause of CFS after the Nevada outbreak.
Patent for diagnosing CFS by 2'-5'A oligonucleotide levels and treating with mismatched double-stranded RNA.

Resting ECG, T-wave integrals, ambulatory rhythm and left ventricular dimensions and shortening were normal, no wall-motion abnormalities, but only 4 of 31 patients vs 20 of 32 controls reached target heart rate and peak heart rate was lower (124 vs 152 bpm).
note: Resting LV size similar to controls

finding: Scanning electron microscopy showed fewer normal discocytes and more cup-shaped red cells in volunteers with ME than controls.
Lifetime psychiatric disorder rates were high in 28 CFS patients and more often preceded fatigue than followed it.
18 of 39 children with prolonged fatigue had Coxsackie B serological evidence and many had muscle complaints; the authors proposed 'fatigue-dysphoria syndrome'.
Only 6 of 135 patients with 6+ months of fatigue met CFS criteria and 67% had active psychiatric disorder.
Raised anti-EBV DNase and DNA polymerase antibodies were found only in patients with VCA titres above 10,000; three such patients developed lymphoma.
Multitest CMI delayed hypersensitivity scores were lower in ME syndrome than matched controls, suggesting a T-cell abnormality.
Patients with EBV early-antigen titres of 1:160 or more did not differ from antibody-negative controls in symptoms, examination, laboratory data or follow-up outcome.
Coxsackie B IgM ELISA was positive in 37% of 290 adults with ME and 38% of 47 children vs 9% of 500 well adult controls; neutralising antibodies were raised in 12.5% of psychiatric inpatients.
note: Serology, single group; not confirmed by later PCR

finding: Enterovirus-specific RNA by slot blot was above normal in muscle biopsies from 20 of 96 patients up to 20 years after onset, with elevated creatine kinase.
note: Not replicated by later PCR studies

finding: Original 1988 CDC working case definition renaming chronic EBV syndrome as chronic fatigue syndrome with major and minor criteria.
Commentary calling ME a misnomer, noting muscle biochemistry does not support a metabolic defect, and aetiology unknown.
Most patients had low NKH1+T3- cell numbers and consistently low cytotoxicity against several targets; IL-2 partly restored killing of K562 but not EBV-infected cells.
67% of patients met major depression criteria and 50% had a prior depressive episode vs non-clinical volunteers.
CBV IgM positivity was 31% in ME vs 9% in controls (myo/pericarditis 33%); cross-reactions with other enteroviruses occurred.
Blood viscosity did not differ significantly, but whole-blood filterability differed in females at low pressure in the acute phase and not in the chronic state.
Cutaneous reflex EMG responses recorded in children with several neurological conditions, ME being one group.
note: ME only one of several groups

finding: Hypothesis that Coxsackie B injury to the dorsal raphe nucleus causes ME with serotonin deficiency.
Coxsackie B neutralising antibody was positive in 16% of suspected ME cases and 41% of well-documented ME vs 4% of normal adults.
In a girls' school outbreak, virology was essentially negative and younger affected girls were more neurotic.
Ten ME patients had a muscle-enzyme and myoglobin pattern resembling Duchenne dystrophy but without raised creatine kinase.
Proposes shared mechanisms between acute disseminated encephalomyelitis and epidemic ME.
EEGs from 48 patients showed modest, variably distributed alterations suggesting disturbed cerebral function.
Review proposing that many benign ME outbreaks were mass hysteria or altered medical perception.
